verdicts.title: recompute silently discards an explicit override for a computed variable that is downstream of another overridden variable in the same call
verdicts.reasoning: Verified from the source at lines 386-402. Line 397 assigns B's value: `values.get(variable).value = val`, and line 398 adds B to `changed_vars`. Line 399 calls `_collect_affected(changed_vars)` which at line 343 seeds `stack = list(changed_vars)` with ALL changed vars including A. At line 346, `self.dependents.get(var, [])` for A returns B's CompiledNode (registered at line 283 in `__post_init__`), so B is added to `affected`. Lines 400-401 then null every affected node: `values.get(node.variable).value = _null` — this nulls B's just-set value. Line 402 `_calculate(affected_nodes, ...)` then recomputes B from A's new value. No guard excludes directly-changed nodes from the null+recompute pass. The finding's logic is sound and the code confirms it.

verdicts.title: QUAL_SEP='.' qualified-name parsing via rsplit('.',1) mis-parses any source or variable name containing a dot
verdicts.reasoning: Verified from the source. Line 94: `QUAL_SEP = "."`. Line 105: `return f"{namespace_name}{QUAL_SEP}{var_name}"`. Line 494: `source_name, variable_name = qual_name.rsplit(QUAL_SEP, 1)`. Line 579: identical pattern in `explain`. The round-trip is only invertible when neither source nor name contains a dot. If a variable name is 'a.b' under source 's', the qual_name is 's.a.b' and rsplit splits at the last dot to give source_name='s.a', variable_name='b', producing a KeyError or wrong lookup. No validation of names against '.' exists at `External.__getitem__` (line 134) or `Variables.__init__` (line 216). The finding's claim and evidence are accurate.
